notes: NWC construction follows Colgate’s definition: working capital = (current assets excluding cash and marketable securities) − (current liabilities excluding short-term debt). For 2023 NWC, balance-sheet components are taken from the 2024 Form 10-K (since 2025 10-K balance sheets only show 2025 and 2024). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))

EBIT is mapped to GAAP Operating profit from Colgate’s consolidated statements/segment reconciliation tables. 2025 operating profit is depressed by discrete GAAP items (impairment, litigation-related items, restructuring/program charges). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))

Tax rate is estimated as the simple average of Colgate’s effective tax rates for 2025 (26.1%) and 2024 (22.9%) because the DCF input requires a single base-case tax rate. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))

Investments is set to marketable securities included in Other current assets at 12/31/2025 (USD 107MM). This is a definition choice; other longer-term equity-method investments are not captured in this field. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))

WACC, terminal growth, and terminal exit EBITDA multiple are base-case valuation assumptions (not explicitly disclosed in the filings) and should be treated as model parameter choices; comps were included mainly for sanity-checking ranges. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/pg/statistics/?utm_source=openai))

NOL utilization percent is assumed (0.80) because the filing discloses NOL balances and valuation allowance context but does not provide a single forward utilization rate suitable for a DCF input. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))

catalysts: Sustained organic sales growth within guidance ranges and mix improvement as competitive dynamics normalize. ([investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-colgatepalmolive-q4-2025-earnings-beat-forecasts-93CH-4476458?utm_source=openai))

Cost savings and productivity execution translating into higher GAAP operating margins versus the 2025 trough. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))
Hill’s Pet Nutrition performance (pricing/volume) driving consolidated operating profit growth. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))
company_overview: Colgate-Palmolive operates in Oral, Personal and Home Care and Pet Nutrition (Hill’s) segments. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))
The company serves consumers in more than 200 countries and territories and reports results in USD. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))

2025 GAAP operating margin was depressed by goodwill/intangible impairment, restructuring-related items, and other discrete charges. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))
current_context: FY 2025 net sales were $20.382B with GAAP operating profit of $3.306B (operating profit margin 16.2%). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))

Management’s FY 2026 guidance referenced net sales growth of 2%–6% and organic sales growth of 1%–4% (with earnings-per-share growth characterized as double-digit). ([investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-colgatepalmolive-q4-2025-earnings-beat-forecasts-93CH-4476458?utm_source=openai))

Colgate also highlighted an updated long-term strategic roadmap alongside FY 2025 results. ([investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/colgatepalmolive-q4-2025-slides-organic-sales-growth-accelerates-new-strategy-unveiled-93CH-4476521?utm_source=openai))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth stays in the low-to-mid single-digit band consistent with management’s 2026 guidance and a gradual return to steadier momentum. ([investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-colgatepalmolive-q4-2025-earnings-beat-forecasts-93CH-4476458?utm_source=openai))

EBIT margin is assumed to normalize toward ~21% as one-time/exception items dissipate versus 2025’s GAAP margin trough. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))

Reinvestment intensity remains disciplined: the company indicated capital expenditures for 2026 expected to be approximately 3.0% of net sales. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))

Working capital is structurally negative under the company’s definition (excluding cash & marketable securities and excluding short-term debt), supporting ongoing free cash flow. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Input cost/FX volatility compressing gross profit and delaying margin recovery. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))

Additional restructuring, litigation, or impairment charges could pressure reported EBIT and cash flows. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))
Working-capital swings (timing of receivables/payables/accruals) reducing free cash flow conversion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021665/000002166526000006/cl-20251231.htm))
